description: GMAT RungeKutta89 reference states cross-validating the Polaris propagator, force composite, and attitude kinematics. Force-model cases (two_body, zonal_j2, third_body) and an orbit-regime matrix (iss_leo, sso_leo, geo, molniya_heo) exercise the propagator from LEO through GEO through a high-eccentricity HEO; attitude_spinner checks the quaternion attitude propagation against GMAT's Spinner.

provenance.note: t_s values are GMAT's reported ElapsedSecs, which overshoot the nominal sampling grid by ~0.4 us; propagate to these exact times. States are EarthMJ2000Eq, converted from GMAT's km/km-s to SI.

cases.name: two_body
cases.description: Circular 500 km equatorial orbit, Earth point mass only, 1.5 orbits.
cases.tolerance_rationale: Pure two-body with Earth.Mu set to wgs84::kGM exactly, so nothing but integrator truncation separates the two propagators; hand-verified agreement is 3.8 mm over 1.5 orbits, and the 5 cm band leaves room for step-control differences.

cases.name: zonal_j2
cases.description: Circular 500 km orbit at 28 deg inclination, degree-2 order-0 zonal gravity (J2 only), 1.5 orbits.
cases.tolerance_rationale: GMAT uses EGM96 and Polaris uses EGM2008; their normalized C20 values differ slightly, and that model difference - not propagator error - dominates the hand-verified 4.7 cm separation over 1.5 orbits. The 0.5 m band is an order of margin on top of it.

cases.name: third_body
cases.description: Circular 500 km orbit at 28 deg inclination, Earth point mass plus Sun and Moon third-body perturbations, ~4 orbits.
cases.tolerance_rationale: GMAT reads DE424 (the closest DE it ships to the DE440 Chebyshev fit Polaris uses) and any residual is that ephemeris difference, not Polaris error. Measured GMAT-vs-Polaris separation over the 4-orbit arc is 3.9 mm; the 0.1 m band is ~25x margin on an ephemeris-model difference.

cases.name: iss_leo
cases.description: ISS-like 417 km circular orbit at 51.6 deg, degree-8 gravity, ~5 orbits.
cases.tolerance_rationale: Degree-8 gravity, EGM96 (GMAT) vs EGM2008 (Polaris): the higher-degree coefficient differences accumulate over five 51.6 deg orbits. The band is model difference, not propagator error — the 2 m allowance is a few x the EGM96/EGM2008 separation at degree 8.

cases.name: sso_leo
cases.description: Sun-synchronous 700 km circular orbit at 98.2 deg, degree-8 gravity, ~4 orbits — the mission template regime, retrograde and near-polar.
cases.tolerance_rationale: Same degree-8 EGM96-vs-EGM2008 model difference as iss_leo, at the near-polar 98.2 deg SSO inclination where the J2 nodal precession the orbit is designed around is strongest.

cases.name: geo
cases.description: Geostationary 42,164 km orbit at 0.05 deg, degree-4 gravity plus Sun/Moon third body and SRP, 1 day — the long-arc SRP/third-body-dominated regime.
cases.tolerance_rationale: A full GEO day is SRP- and third-body-dominated; the residual is the sum of the EGM96/EGM2008 field difference, the DE424/DE440 ephemeris difference (both ~cm), and — by far the largest term — the two SRP models' shadow/flux/area handling over 24 h at GEO (Polaris cannonball vs GMAT spherical). Measured GMAT-vs-Polaris separation peaks at 120 m; the 150 m band gives margin on a model difference, not propagator error, and is <3e-6 relative on a 42,000 km radius.

cases.name: molniya_heo
cases.description: Molniya HEO: 600 x 39,800 km, 63.4 deg, e=0.74, degree-4 gravity plus Sun/Moon, ~2 orbits — the high-eccentricity integrator-stress case.
cases.tolerance_rationale: The e=0.74 orbit sweeps 7,000 km/s at perigee to <1,600 km/s at apogee, so the two adaptive step controllers place their nodes very differently and the RK89 truncation no longer cancels the way it does on a circular orbit — this is the case that stresses step control, not model fidelity. The 25 m band over two ~12 h orbits is <1e-6 relative near apogee.

cases.name: attitude_spinner
cases.description: Torque-free spinner: spherical inertia, initial body rate (2, -1, 3) deg/s about the inertial axes, attitude propagated 300 s. Circular LEO carrier orbit (two-body) so the state history is defined too.
cases.tolerance_rationale: Two-body carrier orbit (position band as two_body). The attitude is a constant-rate rotation both sides compute independently; 1e-3 deg over 300 s covers GMAT's quaternion-report rounding and the small deg/s->rad/s conversion, far below any physical claim.
